reviews.title: Careful! They charge after free trial!!!
reviews.text: Not a great app, only used it two days.  They also charged a ton of money without my approval!!  I signed up for a one month risk free trial, no automatic renewal, but they charged almost forty dollars !!!  More than a full gym membership.  Fraud.

reviews.title: Line dancing
reviews.text: When I ordered it there was an ad on Facebook saying line dancing for a woman over 55 I can't find it anywhere and I can't find a Help button

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: I was charged and did not approve of this charge. How can businesses do this without consequences. That money had better be put back into my account.

reviews.title: No walking involved
reviews.text: Worst exercise app I ever had supposed to be a WalkFit app. All it was with some guy moving his arms. Apparently, it’s something like tai chi. I want to do some exercise not just move my arms.

reviews.title: BEWARE - This App Publisher is VERY skilled at sneak subscription billing
reviews.text:
This App appears free with useful limited features. It does not appear as a free trial that will end. It obtains your default AppleID purchase method without clear warning. It autobills you a 3 month subscription without clear warning. It does not appear in your Apple Subscriptions.

All of these tactics are intentional, deceitful, and should be regulated better by the Apple Store.

Check your profile account subscription settings “in this app” if you did not intend to subscribe.

UPDATE: After reaching out to the “Kate” email, I was refunded 2 of the payments. All would have been best but I’ll take some responsibility for missing that many charges.

UPDATE: My feedback is same as what I emailed. Track users that are inactive and stop billing them.

reviews.title: Scammers!
reviews.text: I have canceled this app and they keep trying to access my account for payment. They will not stop. They have done it seven times and continues be aware.

reviews.title: Unscrupulous business
reviews.text: I got a notice from PayPal that my bank was charged 39.99 for subscription to the service that I did not want. I immediately contacted the company to tell them to cancel it and that I did not want their product as I had no use for it. They told me that there was no way for them to refund my money and sent me an email saying that I approved automatic renewal. If that’s the case, it was somewhere written in very fine print and I never received any notice that it would occur. Then, on top of it all they said they would cancel going forward, but then when I just went to the app, they completely cut off my ability to use the app. So I paid for it. They won’t refund it and they’re not giving me the service that has been paid for that they will not refund. Makes me wonder how many other people this has happened to. Be warned there are better apps out there and better business.

reviews.title: Subscription BEWARE
reviews.text: £88.99 without warning!!! I received a notification from my bank today to let me know that an automated subscription has been taken out of my bank without any prior warning. BEWARE as I am currently disputing this and wish to warn others

reviews.title: Deceptive Practices!
reviews.text: Welltech somehow has managed to build a company by stealing from its customers! I downloaded the app as a FREE APP on the Apple Store with NO INDICATION that I was being subscribed through somehow accessing my Apple Wallet. When I see that I’ve been subscribed I try to find the app in my subscriptions to cancel and get a refund - it’s not there! ALL of my subscriptions are located in my Apple account, yet this one is not. Welltech is a deceptive company and after a quick Google Search I see that many others have been deceived by them. I will NEVER use another Welltech app again. Too many other companies that give you the same results without scamming you.

reviews.title: App is worthless now
reviews.text:
I used to LOVE this app when it connected to my Fitbit/google health app for the step count, however now that it ONLY connects to Apple health the step count is wrong EVERY DAY!!!  I don’t carry my phone with me everywhere/time I walk.  I don’t carry it on my person on the treadmill or into the pool so those steps aren’t counted.  It looks like I am missing my step count when in truth I am over.  

I am very disappointed in this new change and plan to remove the app from my fitness routine.

reviews.title: 1 Star - Cancellation Process Feels Like a Scam
reviews.text:
1 Star - Cancellation Process Feels Like a Scam
The app itself is okay. The 1-star rating is entirely due to my experience with their cancellation process.
I cancelled my subscription through the app and received an email confirming that my subscription would remain active until the end of the current term. Based on that confirmation, I considered the subscription cancelled.
To my surprise, I was charged again on October 12 for a renewal. When I contacted support, the AI chatbot first offered me a one-year extension instead of addressing the issue. I declined and requested a human review.
The response I received was that, according to their records, I had somehow restored the subscription on the same day I cancelled it. I never intentionally reactivated anything. The only reason I logged back into the app was to verify that the cancellation had been processed correctly after receiving the confirmation email.
What I find particularly concerning is that I never received any notification that my subscription had supposedly been reactivated. No email saying "Welcome back" or "Thank you for renewing." Yet they used this alleged reactivation as the basis for refusing a refund.
Their final position was that renewal charges are not eligible for refunds under their policy. My only option was to accept a one-year extension or continue disputing a $66 charge through a process that would likely cost more time and effort than the amount involved.

reviews.text: Unlike most apps, you are given no warning before auto-renew after trial period. You are then asked if you want to sign up to be notified three days ahead of time during next cycle.

reviews.title: They will steal
reviews.text: I downloaded the app, cancelled everything and they still take the money! Not impressed.

reviews.title: Don’t use
reviews.text: At the beginning I paid for the month up front £38.99 & then the £45 which I was led to believe was a discount for the yearly subscription but no only had the app nearly 4 weeks & they took the £38.99 out for the month & another yearly one £79.99. That’s nearly £200 in less than month. I would like a refund for the yearly as I will not be continuing this way too much money. Also there are a lot of glitches when using the app where it would freeze and then lose all the data of the workout you have just completed. I wouldn’t recommend.  Adding to comment- once I complain on here they refunded the yearly cost but I still paid for a month in advance to be able still use as that is still nearly £40 they cut me off already. So I lost £38.99 as can not use app without paying again. I just do not want this to happen to anyone else.

I emailed Walk Fit on the same day asking if they could refund the payment as my wife no longer wanted the subscription. Haven’t heard anything back.

reviews.text: Subscription renewed with no notice at extortionate full price - very poor service requested a refund as definitely not worth the money

reviews.title: Don’t buy
reviews.text: Not worth the cost, a lot better app’s free. The workouts are poor and not properly explained. Can’t emphasise enough this is a waste of money.

reviews.title: Please don’t pay!
reviews.text: This isn’t a personalised programme despite all the upfront questions. It’s a reminder to go for a walk every day and a library of exercises to choose from. I got my money back.

reviews.title: Only on day one
reviews.text: How can I give a review when I’ve just logged in for day one, didn’t give me an opinion to do it later so for that reason I’m giving a one star. Could come back and edit (if given the option to) but for now one star as no option for zero.

reviews.title: App won’t stay open
reviews.text: Can’t get help. Pls someone in customer support help me run this app. I did use it some months ago for a week. I notice you’ve recently taken money from me so thought i would give it another go rather than ask first a refund. The app won’t stay open for more than 2 seconds. reviews.title: Needs clearer instructions
reviews.text: I like the exercise program is short and able to be done at home with no equipment required. However, there are not clear instructions for the individual exercises and by the time I’ve worked out what I am supposed to be doing it has moved on to the next exercise. I signed up for a month subscription and won’t renew which is a shame.

reviews.title: Hidden repeat subscription!
reviews.text: I thought I was paying a one off payment of £9.99 for this App.  However, I’ve now been charged £39.99 on repeat via my credit card. Thankfully I’ve seen this and cancelled the subscription but it wasn’t clear and I’ve lost money. That’s an unbelievable amount to charge for something that isn’t really that good!!

reviews.title: Avoid! Total scam £90 taken without warning
reviews.text: The app is pretty rubbish. I opted for a "one-off" charge for the app which I thought was steep at £20 but 3 months later without warning they've taken £90 out of my bank account. Total scam. I used it for a few days and found it to be total garbage, no way to add previous days steps to the app. I think subscription for this sort of app is just predatory. A one-off cost for a piece of software is transparent & fair. App developers have rushed to embrace the subscription model as they get to make a killing by overcharging on obscure renewals. Thankfully PayPal agreed and fully refunded.

reviews.title: WORST customer service
reviews.text:
I really love the app when it works. If you have an iPhone AND an Apple Watch, it will be great and well worth the subscription. 
If you do not have an Apple Watch, you will need to enter your steps manually- this feature works sometimes and it doesn’t work sometimes which means your streaks will be broken and it will look like you have taken rest days when you haven’t. 
The workouts are great and quick so easy to fit into even a very busy schedule.
I would be giving the app 4 stars even with the frustrating glitches if it weren’t for the inept customer service. I have emailed bak and forth over and over several times and it seems like I am dealing with either AI or someone who is not able to comprehend because they are not reading or understanding what I am trying to explain no matter how many ways or times I explain it. It seems like they read 1 sentence and respond to just that sentence. It is extremely maddening. There is no customer serve number to speak with an actual person .

reviews.title: Integration issues
reviews.text:
I wanted to like this app but cannot recommend based on chronic issue with my data from Fitbit not integrating correctly. My Fitbit app consistently was not working and would constantly read zero steps. The one day it was actually recording my steps in the fitbit app, the WalkFit app did not bring the steps over. I tried all the fixes for Fitbit app to no avail. So, I thought no problem. I will just manually enter my steps into WalkFit. That will be my source of truth. Tonight, I went to look back at my data in WalkFit for the week and found none of manual data was saved anymore. The WalkFit app apparently keeps pulling the zeros over from my malfunctioning Fitbit app. WalkFit should have let me just shut off the Fitbit integration. My only option was to use Apple
Health to get integration with Fitbit to end. I don’t use Apple health. Therefore, I’m now done with the WalkFit app. It’s useless and a waste of $$ now because I can’t track my data in it.

reviews.title: False Advertising
reviews.text:
I purchased this app because the company is advertising tai chi.  I was skeptical because I received two Instagram ads from them, advertising tai chi walking with two different instructors. Now I’m realizing those instructors and interviews were AI.  Still I visited the App Store and saw that they were advertising tai chi walking, so I decided to give it a try and purchase three months of the app.   Even though the App Store pic shows Tai Chi Walking, there is NO tai chi walking. I decided to email customer service with a screenshot showing tai chi walking on the App Store picture.  The Customer Service rep had me send them screenshots of my app workouts.  This is the reply:
“I’ve checked the details again, and unfortunately, the app doesn’t currently offer Tai Chi workouts. I completely understand how useful this feature would be, and I’m sorry for any inconvenience this may cause.
I’ll be sure to pass your feedback along to our team, as we’re always looking for ways to improve the app.”
The company needs to stop claiming they offer tai chi workouts. The next time I see the ad on Instagram, I will screen record it. Also check out the trust pilot reviews for this company.

reviews.title: Horrible App with no morals
reviews.text: I wish I could give no stars. I downloaded this app in June when I was attempted to lose weight after having a baby. After trying the free trial, I cancled the free trial and deleted the app off my phone. The process was not working and I was not feeling like I was getting enough of a workout using the program. Fast forward to last month, October. I randomly was going through my junk mail and saw “you have been charged for the Walk Fit app”. Horrified I went through my bank statements and sure enough, Walk Fit had been still taking money out of my bank account. When attempting to remedy the situation, they of course had no phone number to call and were no help at getting me back the money I had no idea they were taking from me. Do yourself a favor and either use a better, more reliable fitness app that does not have purchases you are unaware of OR just walk yourself because the app is basically just telling you to walk everyday anyway.
